literature_notes: Two ledger lines were evaluated. L1 (PMC1885577) reports enzymatic biotinylation of a full-length PRRG2 construct and flow-cytometric confirmation that the Gla domain is extracellular. Enzymatic biotinylation is a surface-labeling biochemical technique, not an epitope-tag knock-in, fluorescent-protein fusion, transposon/domain-insertion screen, or antibody-epitope insertion; it therefore does not qualify as evidence for a tolerated tag insertion under the ledger rules. L2 (PMC5578492) reports a C-terminal myc-tagged PRRG2 construct expressed in mammalian cells. PRRG2 is a single-pass type-I membrane protein (N-out, C-in): the C-terminus falls in the intracellular domain (residues 131–202 per the authoritative topology landmarks). A C-terminal myc tag is therefore cytoplasmic, not extracellular, and cannot be promoted to a surface-tag site. No ledger line reports a tag insertion at any extracellular position of PRRG2 (residues 24–109) or at the mature N-terminus (after residue 23). Zero surface sites are supported.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal myc tag appended after the last residue (H202) of PRRG2; the C-terminus lies in the intracellular domain (residues 131–202), so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the cell surface.
